other.content: According to a 1996 NGA examination report, underneath the handmade label from An American Place is “a slash and the name Georgia O’Keeffe and the title “Jack in Pulpit-No 2 – 30” penciled in O’Keeffe’s handwriting.” (Source: NGA, 2025)

cr_data.provenance: The artist [1887-1986]; her estate; bequest 1987 to NGA. (Source: NGA, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "No 8 in 1931 exhibition. Ptd. 1930." Abiquiú Notebooks notes backing inscriptions 1, 2 and indicates, "Note: Painting is cracked." Series renumbered by O'Keeffe and Doris Bry in 1970. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Alfred Stieglitz Collection, Bequest of Georgia O'Keeffe, 1987.58.1
description: A large jack-in-the-pulpit plant expands across the frame. A rippling burgundy spathe with glowing green streaks encases the burgundy spadix, or center spike. Bright green leaves frame the plant from below and above. Behind these leaves is a plain, light maroon background.
imageCaption: Courtesy of National Gallery of Art.
title: Jack-in-Pulpit – No. 2
